objective: Decompose HiGS speedup into causal mechanisms
method: Component profiling + ablation (where available) + cross-referencing with existing reports

primary_mechanism.name: Elimination of std indexing_backward + visible-subset gather

evidence.std_profile: Round-10, 21 profiling: std backward includes ~9.8 ms of indexing_backward (gather/scatter for visible subset)
evidence.higs_advantage: Native backward writes directly to master rows via visible_ids; no index_copy_ scatter
evidence.quantification: 9.8 ms / 32.81 ms std backward = 30% of std backward; HiGS saves most of this
evidence.cross_check: Round-21 blend bwd is identical (19.1 ms); SH VJP gap is only ~1.1 ms; remaining gap is indexing

evidence.caveat: This is NOT the speedup vs std; it's the speedup vs the fallback. Vs std's own backward (32.81 ms), native is only -18.9%
evidence.conclusion: Native kernels avoid pipeline re-execution, but the main win vs std is eliminating indexing, not kernel speed

evidence.vs_std: Std SH VJP is 4.89 ms; HiGS is 5.96-6.0 ms (still slower)
evidence.conclusion: Small improvement, but HiGS SH VJP remains slower than std; not a net win

quaternary_mechanisms.name: Python-side optimizations (gather kernel, fused mask, fused Adam)

evidence.gather_kernel: Round 3: 3.79-4.42 ms -> 0.93 ms (-3 ms fwd on bicycle)
evidence.fused_adam: Round 14: optimizer 14.88 -> 6.78 ms (2.2x faster, shared with std)
evidence.conclusion: Important optimizations, but mostly level; std also benefits from fused Adam

culling_reduction.hypothesis: Does culling reduce blend backward work?

evidence.observation: Culled Gaussians generate zero intersections; std also processes zero isects for off-screen/sub-pixel Gaussians
evidence.n_isects_comparison: HiGS n_isects = 14.13M vs std 14.12M on visible subset (round 10)
evidence.conclusion: Culling does NOT reduce blend backward work; the 62.9% culled Gaussians would have contributed zero isects anyway

forward_hierarchy.hypothesis: Does hierarchical forward reduce rasterization cost?

evidence.forward_time: HiGS 17.27 ms vs std 17.92 ms (-3.6%, near parity)

breakdown.rasterize_subset: 10.4 ms (saves ~10.4 ms vs rendering all N)
breakdown.net: 10.4 ms saved - 3.8 ms added = 6.6 ms gross, offset by launch overhead

evidence.conclusion: Forward is at parity; the win is NOT from hierarchical rendering

tile_LOD.hypothesis: Does HiGS macro-tile structure reduce intersection count?
tile_LOD.answer: POTENTIALLY YES, but NOT REALIZED in current implementation

evidence.potential: Round 19: HiGS renderer 8.61 ms vs std 28.99 ms on visible subset (3.37x)
evidence.reality: Current implementation uses standard isect_tiles on visible subset, not HiGS macro-tile
evidence.blocker: Realizing this requires HiGS-format backward consuming macro-tile structure (30M entries vs 330M isects) - substantial rework
evidence.status: Documented but NOT in current numbers

mechanisms: Native gather kernel (avoids PyTorch pathological index_select)
Fused union visibility mask (eliminates double reduction)
Visible-subset rasterization (saves ~10.4 ms, offset by gather+2nd projection)
forward.conclusion: Near parity; not the primary source of end-to-end speedup

mechanisms: Elimination of indexing_backward (~9.8 ms, 30% of std backward)
Direct scatter to master rows (no index_copy_)
Native kernels avoid pipeline re-execution (vs recompute fallback)
Small kernel-level improvements (SH VJP, projection VJP)
backward.conclusion: Primary source of end-to-end speedup; backward is 60% of iteration, so 20% backward saving -> 12% total saving

optimizer.conclusion: Not a HiGS-specific advantage; both arms use fused Adam

counterfactual_analysis.question: If we removed each mechanism, how much speedup would remain?

scenarios.impact: Speedup erased (recompute is +50% slower than std)
scenarios.conclusion: Native backward is NECESSARY for speedup

scenarios.impact: Forward regresses by ~3 ms on bicycle
scenarios.conclusion: Important but not critical; other mechanisms still provide speedup

scenarios.removed: Culling entirely (render all N in HiGS)
scenarios.impact: Lose visible-subset rasterization savings (~10.4 ms fwd), but also lose gather+2nd projection cost (~3.8 ms)
scenarios.conclusion: Culling is NEUTRAL in current implementation; net effect ~parity

key_findings.primary_driver: Backward efficiency (elimination of indexing_backward + native scatter)
key_findings.not_driver: Culling (near-neutral in current implementation); forward hierarchy (at parity)
key_findings.architectural_contribution: Trainable HiGS enables end-to-end differentiation via native backward bound to forward-captured state; this is the contribution, NOT hierarchical rendering speed
key_findings.scaling_behavior: Speedup is FLAT across workload because the mechanism (indexing elimination) is workload-independent

INFERRED: Primary mechanism = indexing elimination (from profile analysis)
HYPOTHESIZED: Tile LOD could provide larger speedup (potential, not realized)
HiGS-format backward could reduce blend bwd (future work)
UNRESOLVED: Why is HiGS SH VJP still slower than std (5.96 vs 4.89 ms)?
Can tile LOD be realized without substantial rework?
